laws.historical_context: The Lebanese Penal Code was enacted on March 1, 1943, by Legislative Decree No. 340, shortly before Lebanon's independence. It replaced the Ottoman Penal Code and was heavily influenced by French criminal law. The Code has been amended numerous times, particularly regarding penalties, corruption offenses, and crimes against children.

laws.historical_context: The Code of Criminal Procedure was enacted by Law No. 328 of August 2, 2001, and published in the Official Gazette on August 7, 2001. It replaced the previous Code of Criminal Procedure of 1948 and subsequent amendments. The new Code was a comprehensive reform of criminal procedure in Lebanon, incorporating international standards and human rights principles. It has been amended multiple times to address emerging issues including trafficking in persons.

laws.historical_context: The Code of Military Justice was enacted by Law No. 24 of April 13, 1968. It establishes the military court system in Lebanon, which includes single military judges, the Permanent Military Tribunal, and the Military Court of Cassation. The military courts have jurisdiction over military personnel for military offenses, as well as over certain crimes committed by civilians, including crimes against state security, terrorism-related crimes, and crimes committed in military premises. The Code has been criticized by human rights organizations for allowing the trial of civilians before military courts and for not fully complying with international fair trial standards.

laws.historical_context: The Special State Security Court was established by Law No. 2/78 of February 15, 1978, during the Lebanese Civil War. It was abolished by Decree No. 603 of May 19, 1983, following the end of the war and the restoration of the regular judicial system.
